─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

+-------------------------------------------+

+------------------+--------+------------------+-----------------------------+
| MOVEMENT         | ERA    | ORIGIN           | CORE THESIS                 |
+------------------+--------+------------------+-----------------------------+
| Arts and Crafts  | 1880s  | Britain          | React vs industrial mass    |
|                  |        | (William Morris) | production; handcraft =     |
|                  |        |                  | truth and beauty            |
+------------------+--------+------------------+-----------------------------+
| Art Nouveau      | 1890-  | France/Belgium   | Nature as ornament; flowing |
|                  | 1910   |                  | organic curves; decorative  |
|                  |        |                  | unity of all arts           |
+------------------+--------+------------------+-----------------------------+
| Constructivism   | 1917-  | Soviet Union     | Art serves revolution;      |
|                  | 1930   | (Rodchenko,      | geometric abstraction;      |
|                  |        |  Lissitzky)      | typography as image         |
+------------------+--------+------------------+-----------------------------+
| De Stijl         | 1917-  | Netherlands      | Pure abstraction: grid,     |
|                  | 1931   | (Mondrian,       | primary colors, horizontal/ |
|                  |        |  van Doesburg)   | vertical only               |
+------------------+--------+------------------+-----------------------------+
| Bauhaus          | 1919-  | Germany          | Art + craft + industry;     |
|                  | 1933   | (Gropius,        | functional beauty; the      |
|                  |        |  Moholy-Nagy)    | school as living experiment |
+------------------+--------+------------------+-----------------------------+
| Swiss / Intl     | 1950-  | Switzerland      | Grid, Helvetica, objectivity|
|                  | 1970   | (Muller-Brockmann| photography over illustr.   |
|                  |        |  Ruder, Hofmann) | universal communication     |
+------------------+--------+------------------+-----------------------------+
| American Modern  | 1940-  | USA              | Corporate modernism; design |
|                  | 1970   | (Rand, Bass,     | as problem-solving; form    |
|                  |        |  Glaser)         | follows function with joy   |
+------------------+--------+------------------+-----------------------------+
| Post-Modern      | 1970-  | USA/Italy        | Rules are for breaking;     |
|                  | 1990   | (Emigre,Cranbrook| multiple layers, irony,     |
|                  |        |  Memphis group)  | historical pastiche         |
+------------------+--------+------------------+-----------------------------+
| Digital Era      | 1990-  | Global           | Screen as primary medium;   |
|                  | present| (Adobe, then web)| UX, interaction, systems    |
+------------------+--------+------------------+-----------------------------+

+------------------------------------------+
|  PRINT DESIGN                            |
|                                          |
|  Editorial: books, magazines, newspapers |
|  Identity: logos, stationery, packaging  |
|  Advertising: posters, billboards        |
|  Signage: wayfinding, environmental      |
|                                          |
|  Technical realities:                    |
|  - CMYK color (not RGB)                  |
|  - DPI: 300 for print, 72 for screen     |
|  - Bleed: 3-5mm beyond trim edge         |
|  - Fonts embedded or outlined            |
|  - PDF/X-1a or PDF/X-4 for press         |
+------------------------------------------+

+------------------------------------------+
|  SCREEN DESIGN                           |
|                                          |
|  Web: responsive layouts, HTML/CSS aware |
|  UI/App: components, states, interaction |
|  Social: fixed-format, thumb-stopping    |
|  Motion: animation, video, broadcast     |
|                                          |
|  Technical realities:                    |
|  - RGB / HEX / HSL color                 |
|  - px for raster, SVG for vector         |
|  - 72/96/144 ppi (Retina = 2x)           |
|  - Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 contrast      |
|  - Design tokens: bridge design to code  |
+------------------------------------------+

blocks.heading_context: ## How Graphic Design Relates to Adjacent Fields
blocks.text:
GRAPHIC DESIGN <-> FINE ART
    Shared: visual language.

  GRAPHIC DESIGN expands into TYPOGRAPHY (in use), which informs
  TYPE DESIGN (making letterforms).
    Shared: grid, type.

  TYPOGRAPHY expands into UI/UX DESIGN, which evolves into
  PRODUCT DESIGN.
    Shared: interaction model.

  UI/UX DESIGN combines with MOTION DESIGN, which uses
  FILM / ANIMATION techniques.
    Shared: time + sequence.
